item.description: - Layouts: save the windows of a workspace with ⌃⌥⇧S and bring them back with ⌃⌥⇧R (your latest saved layout). Up to 9 layouts in the ⛓ menu › Layouts, in Settings › Layouts and with a right click on a workspace in Overview. Restoring moves windows from other workspaces, opens apps that are closed and puts their windows in place as they appear. Optional: hide other apps when restoring. - After a Mac restart, the current workspace is arranged like your latest saved layout. Turn it off in Settings › Layouts. Without a saved layout, Butterfly restores the arrangement from before the restart. - Windows of apps that start late after a restart, or after you unlock the screen, now land in their saved places instead of at the end of the strip. - ⌃⌥T only floats a window of the app in front. With an app that is not on the strip, it does nothing instead of floating another window. - Windows parked at the edge of the screen no longer show a strip there: at most 1 point stays on screen (before up to 10 points, and some apps up to 40).

- In Overview, swipe left or right with four fingers to go to the next or previous workspace. Outside Overview, four fingers left / right still carry the focused column. Needs Raw trackpad touches in Settings › Gestures. - Smoother with Meeting Privacy on: Butterfly does less work behind private-window glass, so screen sharing and clicking in other apps stay responsive.

- Meeting Privacy no longer turns on by itself during calls. To blur private windows automatically in every call, turn it on in Settings › Meeting Privacy. - The tour now shows Meeting Privacy with a switch, so you can turn automatic blur on or off right there. - The shortcuts that cover the window in front or every private app work as before.
